annotations.title: Walkability score for an address or point

description: How walkable one street spot in Europe is (31 countries). Give an address, or lat and lon. Returns the Walkably score from 0 to 100 (60% reach, 40% street quality; a very unpleasant street keeps the score from being high, and a place with nothing in walking distance scores low), the reach and street-quality parts, the share of the country's places it beats, minutes on foot along real streets to each of eight daily needs (groceries, food and drink, shops, health, school, parks, culture, transit) with the nearest place and a Europe-wide verdict, what is inside the nearest parks (a playground, a pitch) with the minutes to the nearest playground, and a link to the spot on the map. Some cells have no street of their own: for those the score is estimated from the cells around them and the answer says so with estimated: true (no country share; any walks come from the nearest measured cell, see needs_from and nearest_measured), and a spot whose streets are cut off from the rest of the street map gets score null and street_island: true (with nearest_measured: the score of the nearest street that is joined, and how far away it is), and a spot we could not join to the streets around it gets score null and cut_off: true. Each score covers a six-sided street cell about 95 m across. Addresses are found with a place search service in the EU that uses OpenStreetMap data. This server is for single places in a conversation. Lists of addresses and bulk use go through the Walkably API: https://walkably.org/business/api/. The US and Canada are not covered yet; to ask for them: https://walkably.org/business/#us-request.

address.description: Street address or place, e.g. "Carrer de Blai 20, Barcelona". Use this or lat and lon.

lat.description: Latitude in degrees (WGS84). Use with lon instead of address.
